territorial_scope.description: Applies to employment decisions made within the City of New York.

evidence.quote: In the city, it shall be unlawful for an employer or an employment agency to use an automated employment decision tool

summary.short: NYC law barring employers and employment agencies from using automated employment decision tools to screen candidates or employees for city employment decisions unless a bias audit within one year, public results summary, and candidate notices are provided. Civil penalties apply; effective 1 January 2023.
summary.long: Local Law 144 of 2021 adds Subchapter 25 to the New York City administrative code, regulating automated employment decision tools (AEDTs): computational processes derived from AI, machine learning, statistical modeling or data analytics that substantially assist or replace discretionary screening of candidates or employees for promotion within the city. Employers and employment agencies may not use an AEDT unless an independent bias audit occurred within one year before use and a summary of results is publicly posted. Candidates and employees residing in the city must receive notice at least ten business days before use, covering the tool and assessed job qualifications, and data information on written request within 30 days. Section 20-872 sets civil penalties of up to $500 for a first violation and $500 to $1,500 for later violations, each day of use a separate violation. Section 20-873 authorizes the corporation counsel to sue to correct violations; § 20-874 preserves private civil actions and Commission on Human Rights enforcement. Effective 1 January 2023.

notes: Text is Int. No. 1894-A as provided (bill form with Be it enacted language); annotation covers this text, not a codified version. Subparagraphs of § 20-871 subdivisions a and b are numbered '1.' repeatedly as printed, while § 20-872(c) refers to paragraphs 1, 2 or 3 of subdivision b. The 'department' that the corporation counsel acts on behalf of in § 20-873 is not named. 'Distribution date' (§ 20-871 a.2) and 'component 1 category' (§ 20-870) are not further defined in the text. Employers and employment agencies are addressees but no specific firms are named. Section 2 sets effect from January 1, 2023.

obligations.summary: Unlawful for an employer or employment agency to use an automated employment decision tool to screen a candidate or employee unless the tool has been the subject of a bias audit conducted no more than one year before its use.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to use of the tool to screen candidates or employees for employment decisions in the city.

enforcement.authority: Tribunal within the office of administrative trials and hearings, or agency of the city designated to conduct such proceedings (§ 20-872(d))
enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of any provision of the subchapter or of any rule promulgated under it, including each day an automated employment decision tool is used in violation of § 20-871(a) and failure to give a notice under § 20-871(b) paragraphs 1, 2 or 3
enforcement.max_penalty_text: not more than $500 for a first violation and each additional violation occurring on the same day as the first violation; not less than $500 nor more than $1,500 for each subsequent violation
enforcement.penalty_formula: Per violation: up to $500 for a first violation and each additional violation on the same day; $500 to $1,500 for each subsequent violation. Each day on which the tool is used in violation is a separate violation of § 20-871(a) (§ 20-872(b)); each failure to give a notice under § 20-871(b) paragraphs 1, 2 or 3 is a separate violation (§ 20-872(c)).
